fees.title: Tenant Fees Act guidance for tenants

structure.title: Renters' Rights Act overview for tenants

deposit_cap.basis: For covered tenancies, the tenancy deposit cap is five weeks of annual rent divided by 52 below GBP 50,000 annual rent, and six weeks at or above GBP 50,000. This checker does not apply the cap above GBP 100,000 or to arrangements outside its supported scope. Never infer protection or authenticity from compliance with this amount cap.

holding_deposit_cap.basis: A holding deposit is distinct from a tenancy deposit. For covered arrangements its cap is one week's rent. Check whether quoted rent and deposit refer to the same tenancy or share. Do not add a holding deposit credited to another payment twice.

prohibited_fee.basis: Mandatory administration, referencing and inventory fees, required professional cleaning and compulsory insurance or service purchases are concerns. Rent, deposits and agreed utilities are not prohibited merely because payable. Tenant-requested changes may cost GBP 50 or evidenced higher reasonable costs. Key replacement must reflect evidenced reasonable cost. Late rent interest requires at least 14 days overdue and is capped at 3 percentage points above Bank Rate annually. Damages must reflect actual loss, not a fixed penalty; do not flag genuine damage liability as a prohibited fee. Distinguish an obligation to return the property clean from a compulsory professional-cleaning payment. Scope excludes ordinary costly commitments.

advance_rent.basis: For covered new assured tenancies, rent cannot be requested or accepted before both parties sign. Between signing and the tenancy starting, the usual maximum required advance is one month's rent for monthly rent or 28 days for weekly rent. Council-arranged homelessness, social and supported arrangements have exceptions and are outside this checker. During a tenancy distinguish voluntary early payment from a compulsory advance. Deposits may be taken before signing; do not apply the rent rule to deposits. Unknown agreement/signing dates require a conditional conclusion.

tenancy_structure.basis: Most existing assured shorthold tenancies converted to assured periodic tenancies on 1 May 2026; covered new private tenancies are periodic. A purported binding fixed end date or section 21 eviction right needs clarification. A heading saying AST alone is not sufficient to allege a breach. Old templates do not establish fraud, and proceedings begun before the change may have transitional treatment.

tenant_notice.basis: For covered new assured periodic tenancies, a landlord cannot require more than two months' tenant notice. Shorter notice may be agreed in writing. Written notice can use different methods; a clause restricting it to one method may need review. Do not conflate tenant notice and landlord possession grounds, which have different rules and exceptions. Pre-May-2026 arrangements need contextual review.

internal_conflict.basis: Compare only operative clauses in the supplied contract. Cite both contradictory obligations. Equivalent units, different parties or address roles are not contradictions. Check definitions, exceptions and explicit amendments before reporting a conflict. This is documentary reasoning, not a legal violation.

missing_schedule.basis: A contract references a material schedule or appendix whose contents were not found in supplied material. Quote the reference and ask for the document. Never claim the document does not exist or that its absence proves illegality. Check whether an appendix with a different heading actually supplies the referenced material.

unusual_obligation.basis: Only report a supported potential conflict with the supplied rules, such as transferring the landlord's structural, heating or wiring repair duty to the tenant irrespective of fault, or a punitive fixed charge. A tenant can remain liable for damage they caused. Ignore merely expensive, inconvenient or unusual commitments without a supported legal issue. Cite the relevant rule and actual obligation; avoid speculative legal claims.
